Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10150 at 15 FR 5219 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed August 11, 1950; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the August 12, 1950 issue. Inventory corrected: two clauses, offsets 3872 to 4182 and 11762 to 12623 of the held text. The text layer interleaves the order with unrelated Federal Register page text (a contents list) between its first and second parts, so the order's operative text is the first part (the enacting words) and the continuation, which are contiguous in the printed order. The dossier's span includes the interleaved unrelated page text. The order's heading and recitals precede the first part and contain no command. Text: The order recites that disputes exist between the Atlantic & East Carolina Railway Company and certain other carriers designated in a list A attached to the order, and certain of their employees represented by the sixteen cooperating non-operating labor organizations designated in a list B attached to the order. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the disputes; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; directs that each carrier involved be given independent consideration and that the labor organizations be permitted to function as a unit before the board; permits the board, to the extent it deems necessary or desirable, to make separate and independent findings with respect to each carrier involved; and, as provided by section 10, it bars any of the carriers involved or their employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the disputes arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Lists A and B (the carriers and the labor organizations) follow the signature block in the held text; they identify the parties and are not separate commands. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 10150 describes creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10150_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10150_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_519666f265.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a cover page dated September 9, 1950. The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking September 9, 1950 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on September 9, 1950 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to October 9, 1950 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. The dossier has no citable record covering the report's date line, so the report date is stated here and is not entered as a later event. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order.
